{"self_assessment": "Impact: I carried the top line of the fish from the middle of the back, round the curve and down to the nose, so the bottom line could start. I then took the tail from the peak of the bump down to the tip, laying the final stretch of the outline. Before the push, the run connected 116 of the 119 standing dominoes to the start, and my two stretches were a large part of the outline.

Execution: I inspected the joins repeatedly instead of assuming they held. I stood a stray domino back up in the belly seam, nudged a jammed domino in the tail, and closed the small gap at the very tip. I kept my building in step with the clock and stopped touching the table before the push so nothing got bumped.

Collaboration: I agreed to the fish plan early and said openly which stretches I would take and which I would stay off, to avoid bumping others' hands. I took on the handoffs at the top line and the tail when asked, and I reported what I found as I went so the table could plan around it.

Leadership: When the top line was slow to reach the nose, I volunteered to take it so the bottom line could start. I offered to take the tail from the peak before anyone asked. I kept my updates short and clear, and I called hands-off at the end so the table stood back for the push.", "my_share_percent": 28}
